messages:
maria_research: heads-up — citrine-v0-int4 onboarding metrics show a jump in structured-output noncompliance from 0.8% -> 6.4% on our tool-invoke eval set since yesterday's rollout. Anyone else seeing this? :eyes:

sanjay_sre: saw spikes in parsing errors in prod canaries, same time window. mostly missing commas / top-level field rename ("result" vs "output"). sample below.

ellie_ml: dropping one of the raw payloads we captured from the canary, looks like truncation + field aliasing:

```\n{
  "id": "req_1234",\n  "tool": "search",\n  "result": {\n    "items": [\n      {"title": "..."}\n    ]\n  } // missing closing array/bracket in some cases\n```

aaron_prod: hypothesis: int4 quantization changed token boundaries around tool markers -> some early stops/merges produce the alternate key name and occasionally drop a final bracket. could be decoder sampling mismatch between quant and fp16.

ellie_ml: quick repro plan: run bench-bot harness comparing fp16 vs citrine-v0-int4 on the same prompt seeds and deterministic decode to isolate tokenization differences. I'll run 1k seeds tonight.

bench-bot: perf/parse-test finished: 1000 requests; schema_fail=61; avg_latency=123ms; model=citrine-v0-int4; commit=fa3b2e9; dashboard: /dash/inf/parse-regress/citrine-int4 (posted).

maria_research: proposed immediate mitigations:
1) add alias mapping for top-level name mismatches (result->output) for 48h to reduce customer impact
2) attempt a single "parse-heal" retry for common defects: insert closing bracket, fix trailing commas, then re-run JSON parse once
3) run a controlled fp16 vs int4 decode comparison and if fail rate persists, promote rollback to previous quant profile.

jenna_docs: can we document the aliasing rule and the temporary parse-heal behavior in the onboarding checklist and release notes? will file a short blurb.

ops-bot: ticket INF-4821 created and assigned to @ellie_ml. Canary rollback alert rule updated: if schema_fail > 5% sustained over 15m, trigger auto-rollback.

sanjay_sre: small caution — don't let parse-heal obscure real model regressions. prefer alias mapping + single retry + verbose logging of the raw model output so ML can inspect.

ellie_ml: ack. will run experiments tonight and post raw diffs + sample tokens. quick command I used to repro: 

```curl -sS -X POST https://api.redwood.com/v1/invoke \\  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \\  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \\  -d '{"model":"citrine-v0-int4","prompt":"[toolcall test]","stream":false}'```

maria_research: thanks all. if bench results show the issue is deterministic in int4, we'll pause rollout and open a quant rollback. otherwise we'll run the alias+one-retry mitigation and monitor. drop any fast parse-healer snippets here if you have them. :thumbsup:
